newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian Broadcasting Corp Morning Update.
newsitem.headline: Australian Broadcasting Corp Morning Update.

text.p: SECT LEADER WARNS OF WORM PLAGUE
There are further bizarre allegations about the sect known as the Magnificat Meal Movement, at Helidon, west of Brisbane.
A former member says sect leader and self-styled prophet Debra Geileskey and her real estate agent husband, Gordon, sell expensive medications to followers.

Angela Jones, who was involved with the sect for four years, says Mrs Geileskey told followers earlier this year a plague of worms would be coming, and that treatments usually given for worms would not work.
Ms Jones says the Geileskeys are selling their special mixture for about $50 a bottle and a lot of people are taking it.
Debra Geileskey has confirmed a special worm treatment was sold at her sect headquarters, known as The Shrine, in Helidon.
But Mrs Geileskey says she encourages people to grow herbs and make the mixture themselves.
"We had to do some worming so to speak in the area when we came here," she said.
"And god was kind, he told us how to do it and we used wormwood and honey and pumpkin seeds and we used cloves."
Mrs Geileskey says they made the mixture themselves, before discovering a similar commercially made worm mixture, which they sold.
THESE BOOTS ARE MADE FOR PRESIDENTIAL WALKING
Crocodile skin boots promised to the U.S. President during his Australian visit are finished, and today the South Australian Premier will present them to the politican who took the order.
Crocodile farmer and Member for the far north Queensland seat of Leichhardt, Warren Entsch, is in Adelaide to take delivery of the boots made at the R.M. Williams factory.
Mr Entsch says the crocodile skin boots with kangaroo skin uppers will go on display in Cairns before he takes them to Washington to see if the boots fit.
"They're top boots, they're high boots and it's an RM Williams size 11 and half G," he said.
Mr Entsch says he watched the bootmakers yesterday put the soles onto the boots and stamp the size onto them, so they're very identifiable.
PROTESTERS EXPECTED TO PICKET PM'S VISIT TO NORTH QLD
Prime Minister John Howard can expect a rowdy welcome this morning when he turns up for a Cabinet meeting in Townsville.
Protesters against the Port Hinchinbrook resort development near Cardwell, between Townsville and Cairns, are expected to picket the meeting.
Native Title and gun control also remain big issues in the north.
Mr Howard may have to defend his policies on two talkback radio sessions prior to the Cabinet meeting, which is being held in the Office of the Premier in Townsville's commerical heart.
Later, Police reinforcements will be located at the picturesque Queens Park where Cabinet will be having an openair lunch.
Five hundred locals from the Seat of Herbert have been invited to the event. They have paid $35 for the privilege.
The local Labor Party is holding a "battlers barbecue" next door at the same time.
HIJACKER ORDERED TO REPORT TO IMMIGRATION
Convicted American hijacker Lorenzo Ervin has been ordered to report to Immigration Department officials in Brisbane this afternoon.
There have been calls to cancel the former Black Panther activist's Australian visa, following claims he's a terrorist and should not be allowed in the country.
Mr Ervin told AM, he and his solicitor are unsure about what will happen when he meets Immigration officials, but they fear he could be deported.
"In fact we've been told that they have not lifted my visa. So I don't know, we were kind of in the dark about what their intentions are. He thinks I'm going to be arrested," Mr Ervin said.
ACTU PROMISES SUPPORT FOR STRIKING MINE WORKERS
ACTU President, Jenni George, says unions affiliated with the mining industry will continue to take a stance against corporate giant, Rio Tinto.

Yesterday, striking workers at the Hunter Valley Number one mine succeeded in blocking a train which had been chartered by the mine management to take 3,000 tonnes of coal from the mine to the Port of Newcastle.
Ms George told striking workers that they could expect support from the ACTU and mining industry unions.
She says the workers at Hunter Valley One are standing up for the rights of miners across Australia.
MCLACHLAN SAYS AUSTRALIA CAN NOT DO WITHOUT AWACS
The Defence Minister Ian McLachlan says the Government is yet to decide the future of plans to extend the surveillance of Australia's Northern coastline.
Numerous options for the establishment of an Airbourne Early Warning And Control System have been considered over the past 20 years, including remote controlled 'sentry' aircraft.
Mr McLachlan says Cabinet has not yet made a decision on whether such a system will be funded, but he says Australia can not do without the surveillance enhancing system.
The Minister says it is a high prority for the Government, adding that air battles can not be run properly without one.
ONE NATION DIRECTOR SAYS PROTEST THE WORST HE HAS SEEN
One man is unconscious in hospital and police intend to charge 10 people, after violent protests against Pauline Hanson's One Nation party at Dandenong in Suburban Melbourne.
About 1,500 protestors were involved with up to 100 police protecting Dandenong Town Hall and the local police station.
Scuffles broke out between police and the demonstrators.
Glass bottles were thrown and protestors were wrestled to the ground.
About 200 One Nation supporters were pelted with eggs, tomatoes and Balloons filled with Urine as they entered the meeting to form Victoria's first suburban branch of the Party.
One Nation National Director, David Ettridge, says the demonstration was the worst he has seen.
Mr Ettridge says compared it to a previous protest in newcastle, in New South Wales.
He says protestors there were better behaved, even in the attendance of One Nation Party leader, Pauline Hanson.
He says last night in Melbourne was huge rally of people without anyone there important enough to protest against.
UNLICENSED RAVE PARTIES MAY BE OUTLAWED IN QUEENSLAND
The Queensland Health Minister, Mike Horan, says he expects to take a submission to Cabinet by the end of this month outlawing unlicensed rave parties and designer drugs such as Fantasy.

Mr Horan says tests are yet to confirm if four people who overdosed at a house at Merrimac, on the Gold Coast today, took Fantasy, but it appears it was the same drug which caused the collapse of 10 people outside a nightclub earlier this year.
He admits there is nothing the Government can do to police private parties where people are taking the drug, but the package does contain measures to educate people about its dangers.
Mr Horan says there needs to be some degree of regulation relating to public dance parties.
Meanwhile, four people remain in hospital on the Gold Coast following the overdose.
Two men and a woman remain on life support systems, and another man is in the Observation Ward.
Police have charged a 33-year-old man with possession of a dangerous drug.
